best_for: Engineers, students and scientists who want a desktop calculator that handles units, currencies and symbolic math instead of switching to a full math package.
description:
Qalculate! is a desktop calculator written by Hanna Knutsson. Instead of pressing one button at a time, you type a whole expression, with numbers, functions, variables, matrices and dates mixed in, and the answer updates as you type.

Results can show as exact values, decimals, or simple and mixed fractions, in any number base, even Roman numerals. The history list lets you add comments, search, and reuse old results in new sums. You can build your own functions and variables from the menus, import and export CSV data, look up chemical elements in a built-in data set, and convert between calendars. Version 5.13 added ymd(), which counts the years, months and days between two dates.

points.title: Units, currencies and algebra
points.text: Qalculate! knows over 400 units, converts currencies with daily updated rates, carries physical constants, and solves equations and integrals symbolically, with arbitrary precision and uncertainty tracking.

points.title: Plots need Gnuplot
points.text: Graphs of functions and data are drawn with Gnuplot. The project lists Gnuplot as an optional dependency that is needed only for plotting.

points.title: Two interfaces and a CLI
points.text: The Windows installer includes both the GTK and Qt interfaces and the command-line version. It needs Windows 10 version 1809 or later and installs for the whole machine. A portable zip keeps all its data in its own folder.

points.title: Linux: Flathub is the author's pick
points.text: The download page recommends the Flatpak. The Qt build listed here is verified on Flathub; a separate GTK build exists under its own ID. Linux shows 5.13.0 while Windows is on 5.13.2.

points.title: No Mac build from the project
points.text: There is no official macOS download. The project points Mac users to MacPorts and Homebrew, which is why this site lists only Windows and Linux.

points.title: Free, but no guarantees
points.text: It is GPL-2.0 or later and free. The author asks for bug reports and states that no guarantees are given.

points.title: Versions here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 50 versions; Linux lists only the current release.
